questions.stem: A provincial health office is planning to allocate additional physicians. Region A has lower physicians per 10,000 population, while Region B has higher outpatient visits per physician and longer waiting times. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate data-driven decision?

choices.A: Allocate physicians to Region A based on physician-to-population ratio
choices.B: Allocate physicians to Region B based on workload indicators
choices.C: Allocate physicians equally to both regions
choices.D: Delay decision due to conflicting data
choices.E: Make a data-driven decision based only on hospital numbers

questions.stem: A new vaccine is highly effective in preventing an aging-related condition. However, the public shows low interest because it is not perceived as a disease. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.A: Increase vaccination coverage through targeted communication as a data-driven decision
choices.B: Do not implement the vaccine because it is not a disease
choices.C: Limit vaccination only to high-risk hospitalized patients
choices.D: Delay the program until public demand increases

questions.stem: Doctor A cites strong results of drug A from an RCT, while Doctor B argues that in real practice many patients discontinue due to side effects. Which principles are being used?

questions.stem: After introducing an effective treatment, which indicators are expected to decrease?
Widespread mask use would most directly reduce which indicator?
COVID-19 vaccination is most likely to reduce which indicators?
Which additional indicator BEST assesses physician adequacy?

choices.A: Number of hospital beds per hospital

questions.stem: A study shows that people in lower socioeconomic groups have consistently worse health outcomes (higher morbidity and mortality) compared to higher socioeconomic groups, and the difference follows a stepwise pattern across all income levels. What is this phenomenon called?

Country X has eliminated absolute poverty — everyone can afford food, shelter, and basic healthcare. However, income inequality remains high (top 20% earn 15× more than bottom 20%). A clear social gradient in health still exists: wealthier people live longer and have fewer chronic diseases. A policymaker claims: “Since no one is poor anymore, income inequality should no longer affect health.” Which concept BEST refutes this argument?

choices.A: Relative poverty: social comparison causes chronic psychosocial stress that affects health even when basic needs are met
choices.B: Absolute poverty: some citizens still cannot afford healthcare
choices.C: Social exclusion: wealthy groups exclude poorer groups from society
choices.D: Health literacy: wealthier people understand health information better
choices.E: Physical environment: richer areas have better living conditions

questions.stem: A rural district reports methamphetamine use disorder prevalence of 18% among men aged 18–35. The area also has high unemployment (60%), high school dropout rate (45%), no mental health services within 80 km, and long-term economic decline after mining industry collapse. The district health officer proposes focusing only on law enforcement and rehabilitation clinics. A public health consultant argues this is insufficient. Which response BEST supports the consultant’s position?

choices.A: Rehabilitation clinics should be relocated to urban centers for cost-efficiency
choices.B: Law enforcement is harmful and should be completely removed
choices.C: Addressing addiction requires upstream action on social determinants of health (unemployment, education, mental health access, economic conditions) in addition to treatment
choices.D: Traditional healers should replace psychiatric care due to cultural reasons
choices.E: Addiction is mainly genetic, so intervention programs will have limited impact

questions.stem: Which indicator best assesses the effectiveness of preparedness and response during an outbreak?

choices.B: Number of completed contact tracing cases
choices.D: Time from symptom onset to isolation

questions.stem: Which analytic study design is MOST commonly used in foodborne outbreak investigations and why?

choices.A: Randomized Controlled Trial: gold standard for evidence
choices.B: Cohort Study: best for measuring incidence rates
choices.C: Case-Control Study: fast and efficient when cases are already identified
choices.D: Cross-sectional Study: best for prevalence measurement
choices.E: Ecological Study: best for population-level comparisons

questions.stem: A doctor is reviewing several studies to decide the best treatment for patients. He wants to use evidence that summarizes results from multiple studies to increase reliability. Which type of study should he choose?
A graph shows that children born to mothers with low socioeconomic status have poorer health outcomes. Which is the MOST appropriate government intervention based on Social Determinants of Health?

choices.A: Provide high-quality nutrition for pregnant women to improve fetal health
choices.B: Distribute free diapers to families with infants
choices.D: Focus only on treating sick children

questions.stem: A study shows that people in lower socioeconomic groups have consistently worse health outcomes (higher morbidity and mortality) compared to higher socioeconomic groups, and the difference follows a stepwise pattern across all income levels. What is this phenomenon called?

A country is considering reducing sugar tax to improve affordability of beverages. However, public health officials are concerned about increasing obesity and diabetes rates. If the government decides to proceed with a health-protective approach, where should they BEST start?

choices.A: Eliminate all taxation on sugar-sweetened beverages immediately
choices.B: Increase hospital capacity for diabetes management
choices.C: Gradually reduce tax while simultaneously implementing health promotion and monitoring consumption trends
choices.D: Focus only on treating obesity cases in hospitals
choices.E: Shift responsibility entirely to individual behavior change

questions.stem: A patient is referred from a primary care clinic to a large hospital with specialist physicians for further diagnosis and treatment. This level of care is BEST classified as?
A country wants to improve efficiency in its healthcare system and reduce unnecessary hospital visits. What is the MOST appropriate strategy?

choices.B: Strengthen primary care as first contact point

questions.stem: In Norway’s health system, what is the MAIN role of general practitioners (GPs)?

choices.B: Act as gatekeepers to specialist and hospital services

questions.stem: Which statement best describes hospital access in Japan’s health system?

choices.A: Strict gatekeeping system requiring referral before hospital care
choices.B: Free access to hospitals without gatekeeping under social health insurance
choices.C: Access limited to private hospitals only
choices.D: Hospital care requires full out-of-pocket payment

questions.stem: A country has a health system where all citizens are required to purchase basic health insurance from private insurers. The government regulates benefits and pricing, and individuals pay premiums directly. Which health system model does this most closely represent?
Germany has a social health insurance system associated with high costs and potential overutilization of healthcare services. What is the most appropriate method to control demand-side utilization?
Which intervention BEST improves equity in healthcare access?
According to the Ecology of Medical Care, the largest proportion of health problems in a population occurs in which setting?
Patients with mild illness bypass primary care and directly seek care at tertiary hospitals. What is the main health system problem?
Which statement BEST distinguishes health promotion from primary prevention?

choices.A: Health promotion focuses on treating early disease, while primary prevention focuses on rehabilitation
choices.B: Health promotion aims to improve overall health and well-being, while primary prevention aims to prevent specific diseases
choices.C: Health promotion is limited to vaccination programs only
choices.D: Primary prevention is only about hospital-based care
choices.E: Both are the same concept with different names

questions.stem: A community has a rising prevalence of childhood obesity. The local government decides to build a public exercise park to encourage physical activity among children. Which level of prevention does this intervention represent?
The government increases tobacco tax to reduce smoking in the community. Which action area of the Ottawa Charter does this represent?
A health education campaign teaches people practical skills to improve their diet and physical activity. According to the Ottawa Charter, this strategy mainly reflects?

A physician advises a patient that exercise reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease. The patient believes it is beneficial but feels it is difficult to start due to lack of time. According to the Health Belief Model, which construct does this represent?

A physician asks a 45-year-old smoker about quitting. The patient says: “I know smoking is bad, and I’ve been thinking about quitting — maybe in the next few months — but I’m not ready to set a date yet.” Based on the Transtheoretical Model, which stage and management is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Precontemplation: provide basic information about smoking risks
choices.B: Contemplation: explore ambivalence and help him weigh pros and cons of quitting
choices.C: Preparation: help him set a quit date and develop an action plan
choices.D: Action: provide relapse prevention strategies and social support

questions.stem: A 45-year-old smoker says: “I know smoking is harmful, and I’ve been thinking about quitting, but I feel I don’t have enough time and confidence to start.” According to Social Cognitive Theory, which is the MOST appropriate intervention?

choices.A: Increase perceived severity by emphasizing complications
choices.B: Improve self-efficacy by setting small achievable goals
choices.C: Provide financial incentives to quit smoking
choices.D: Enforce strict regulations on tobacco use
choices.E: Ignore patient readiness and advise immediate cessation
